$comment: Written reasons for the capabilities catalogue (docs/DSL_CAPABILITIES.html), batch 10 of N, 2026-11-23 (REG-357, owner: do only 20% of the remaining cases, of mixed complexity). One reason per keyword: what need it serves and why a lower rung of the extension ladder (expression, function, flow step, hand-written code) or an existing keyword cannot do it. The reasons state the need, not the evidence counts: the catalogue's own columns show samples, tests and examples and change as the corpus grows, so a count written here would go stale. The batch is every 5th keyword still without a reason, taken within each kind of value (boolean, text, number, choice, list, object, reference) so simple and complex ones are mixed. Key = slot id exactly as the catalogue shows it; the generator refuses a reason for a keyword the schema does not have.

reasons.presentationMetadata.offlineWrite: A person in a warehouse or on the road may lose signal while entering records; declaring a concept offline-writable lets the generated screen queue creates and updates and replay them on reconnect, and a queued update that finds the row changed meanwhile is refused and kept for the person to redo, never silently overwriting, which a hand-written screen would have to rebuild for every concept.
reasons.invariant.type: A concept rule is either a uniqueness rule over a set of fields or a condition that must hold; the type says which, so the platform enforces it the same way on every write path instead of each screen checking its own.
reasons.externalAi.providers: A company may reach AI models through its own gateway or a self-hosted server that the shipped catalogue does not list; this declares such an endpoint for this app only, it must still be listed in vendors to be called, and its key is always read from the environment variable derived from its id, so a model can never point an endpoint at another provider's key.
reasons.pack:roles: A pack whose feature needs roles, such as an approver, must bring them; listing the roles in the pack, in place or from a model file, installs them with the feature, so each app does not declare them again and the pack's permissions have someone to be granted to.
reasons.root:roles: An app must say what kinds of user exist and what each may do; the roles list is that declaration, and every screen, action and flow that names a role refers back to it, so access is decided in the model and not scattered in code.
reasons.query.limit: A screen or an AI agent should never pull a whole table; the limit caps the rows a query returns, so a heavy query stays safe however large the data grows.
reasons.inboundDoor.signature: Outside services sign their deliveries in different ways, GitHub with a hex HMAC, Shopify with a base64 one, Stripe with a timestamped value; the scheme names which style to verify, with the platform's own style as the default, so a delivery is accepted only when its signature matches the way its sender signs.
reasons.flow.input: A flow that creates, updates, deletes or queries a record should take the record's shape as its input; declaring the input like a concept body, with a mode, makes the flow's contract follow the concept instead of copying its fields, so a change to the concept reaches the flow.
reasons.appShellNavItem.target: A menu entry must lead somewhere; the target names the concept or panel it opens, and an entry with no target is a heading that groups others, so the menu is declared with the app and not hard-coded in a page.
reasons.conversion.with: When a migration merges two old fields into one, such as first and last name, the pieces need a separator between them; this text goes between each pair and defaults to none, so a merge needs no hand-written SQL to join them.
reasons.flowHook.targetStep: A pack or a team that wants to add a step to a flow it does not own, such as an extra check before saving, must say where; the target names the step of the base flow the hook attaches to, with a position before or after it, so the base flow stays untouched and the extension is declared beside it.
reasons.guidePageGadget.x: A chart of sales per month needs to know which query column makes the categories along the bottom; naming it picks the x axis, so one query serves a chart without reshaping its data.
reasons.panelAction.contentType: An action that hands the person a file, such as an export, must tell the browser what kind of file it is, for example text/csv, so it is opened or saved correctly; it is required for a download result, so a file never arrives with a missing or wrong type.
reasons.presentationMetadata.readonlyWhen: A field should stop being editable once a condition holds, such as an invoice that is already paid; an expression over the record makes the control read-only in the screen while it is true, so the rule lives with the field and not in a custom screen script.
reasons.schemaObject.defaultExpression: A boundary schema, such as a flow or capability input, often has a value that should fill in when the caller sends none, such as a discount of zero; the expression gives that default, so every caller gets the same fill-in and no step has to add it.
